text:
mike_support: Customer reports service endpoint `svc-internal.redwood.com` started returning NXDOMAIN from app pods in prod VPC after a recent egress allowlist change. They say other VPCs are fine. Here's the minimal repro we have from a pod:

mike_support: dig svc-internal.redwood.com +short @172.31.0.2 -> (empty)
mike_support: dig svc-internal.redwood.com @8.8.8.8 -> 203.0.113.42
mike_support: curl -v https://svc-internal.redwood.com/ -> TLS handshake: certificate CN=elb.amazonaws.com, remote IP 203.0.113.42

mike_support: So looks like DNS for the private hosted zone is not being resolved locally and traffic is egressing to public, hitting a public ELB with a public cert (hence TLS mismatch). Customer says they recently tightened egress rules to only allow a small set of IPs/ports.

julia_infra: can you paste the pod /etc/resolv.conf and the VPC DHCP options? also which VPC endpoint type is this (interface vs gateway)?

mike_support: resolv.conf:
nameserver 172.31.0.2
search ip-172-31-0-aws.internal
options ndots:5

mike_support: It's an AWS interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-xxxxx) fronting our internal svc. Private hosted zone = svc.private.redwood.com associated to the prod VPC only.

sam_eng: quick checks: 1) ensure outbound UDP/53 to VPC resolver (base+2) isn't blocked by egress rules. 2) ensure interface endpoint ENI IPs (the endpoint has ENIs in subnets) are reachable on 443. If DNS queries are blocked, node will forward to public resolvers or fall back, or the app might do a public lookup depending on library.

leo_networks: also check any central fw or NAT GW rules that might rewrite DNS to corporate forwarders. If you allow only specific CIDRs, the ENI IPs of the interface endpoint are in the VPC CIDR — double-check security group egress and the network policy that was applied.

mike_support: Checking SGs now. Pod -> node local ip -> nat -> internet. Egress policy applied via our cluster egress controller denies outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 except whitelisted. Looks like we allowed 443 to a few trusted IPs, but not the interface endpoint ENI IPs (which are ephemeral). We also didn't allow UDP/53 to the VPC resolver.

julia_infra: that matches the symptom. Route53 private zones resolve only via the VPC resolver. If UDP/53 to 172.31.0.2 is blocked, you'll get no answer and the resolver or app may fallback. The public 8.8.8.8 result is the public record for the public service.

sam_eng: commands to run for root cause: from node (not just pod) run:

# check reachability to VPC resolver
$ nc -u -v 172.31.0.2 53 || echo "udp53 unreachable"
# tcp DNS (some libs use TCP fallback)
$ nc -v 172.31.0.2 53 || echo "tcp53 unreachable"
# curl directly to endpoint ENI IP:443
$ curl -v https://<ENI_IP>/ --resolve "svc-internal.redwood.com:<port>:<ENI_IP>"

sam_eng: and validate the route53 hosted zone association: console or aws cli `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name` + `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids <id>` to confirm association.

mike_support: ran the checks: UDP/53 to 172.31.0.2 is blocked by cluster egress policy; TCP/53 is also blocked. ENI IPs are unreachable on 443 from pods because we only allowed 443 to a few public provider IP ranges.

leo_networks: fix options: 1) Add explicit egress allow for the VPC resolver (VPC_CIDR_base+2) UDP/53 and TCP/53 from nodes. 2) Allow TLS to interface endpoint ENI IPs (but ENIs can change) — better: allow egress to the interface endpoint security group or VPC prefix list. In AWS you can reference the VPC endpoint's security group as destination for SG rules. Alternatively use AWS-managed prefix list for the region or allow the VPC CIDR for intra-VPC traffic.

mike_support: customer tried adding 172.31.0.2:53 allow and re-deployed one pod, dig now returns the private IP: `10.100.200.7` (private service IP). curl now completes and cert CN matches `svc-internal.redwood.com` — TLS good.

mike_support: they still saw intermittent failures for a subset of pods in private subnets. Found cluster egress controller uses IP masquerade on some nodes and DNAT rewrites dest for specific pod ranges -> that cluster rule was still sending DNS to a forwarder we had left in the allowlist. We removed the overwritten forwarder route and everything stabilized.

julia_infra: good catch. TL;DR root cause: overly restrictive egress allowlist blocked VPC resolver + interface endpoint ENI connectivity -> DNS fell back to public resolution / public ELB -> TLS mismatch. Secondary issue: cluster-level IP rewrite to a corporate forwarder that was still allowed.

mike_support: resolution steps we gave customer:
- Allow UDP/TCP 53 to VPC resolver (VPC base+2) in cluster egress rules
- Allow HTTPS (443) to the interface endpoint security group or add VPC ENI IP ranges to allowlist (or allow intra-VPC CIDR)
- Remove legacy DNAT to corporate forwarder for pod ranges or ensure forwarder can resolve private hosted zones via VPC association
- Validate with `dig @172.31.0.2 svc-internal.redwood.com +short` and `curl --resolve` for TLS check

mike_support: customer applied changes at 14:42 UTC and confirmed service restored at 14:46 UTC.

leo_networks: good to document a playbook entry: "private hosted zone resolution fails after egress tightening" with the quick checklist above + sample iptables/egress controller rules to allow VPC resolver. I'll add to infra runbook. :memo:

deploy-bot: deploy 2634f8 -> infra/runbooks updated by leo_networks :white_check_mark:

mike_support: closing the ticket with customer note and fix steps. thanks all :tada:
